nodes.name: Poll Schedule (Every 5 Min)
nodes.notes: Polls on a fixed 5-minute cadence. The workflow tracks its own last-checked watermark externally, so the exact interval isn't load-bearing -- a missed or delayed tick just means a slightly wider window on the next run.

nodes.name: Manual Check Webhook
nodes.notes: On-demand trigger for 'run the monitor right now', e.g. right after deploying a fix, with an optional {force:true} to bypass the poll lock.

nodes.name: Acquire Poll Lock
nodes.notes: Atomic compare-and-set lock with a 600s TTL. The TTL is the safety net for the case this workflow crashes mid-cycle: a stuck lock self-expires instead of deadlocking every future poll forever.

nodes.name: Evaluate Lock Result
nodes.notes: force:true intentionally lets a manual run proceed even without the lock -- useful for an operator who knows the previous cycle is actually stuck, not just slow. It's a deliberate escape hatch, not a bug.

nodes.name: Compute Poll Window
nodes.notes: Falls back to a 15-minute lookback on first-ever run (no watermark yet) rather than scanning the instance's entire execution history.

nodes.name: Fetch Failed Executions Page
nodes.notes: n8n's execution list endpoint is cursor-paginated; a busy instance mid-incident can easily have more failures than one page, so this loops rather than silently only ever seeing the first page.

nodes.name: Fetch Page OK?
nodes.notes: If the n8n API itself is unreachable, that's the monitor's own dependency failing -- treated as a distinct 'monitor degraded' condition, never silently counted as 'zero failures found'.

nodes.name: More Pages?
nodes.notes: pages_fetched < 20 is a safety cap (2000+ failed executions in one window) against an infinite loop if the API ever returns a cursor that never terminates.

nodes.name: Assess Failure Batch
nodes.notes: 5+ distinct workflows failing in the same window smells like a shared dependency outage, not 5 unrelated bugs. Treated differently below: one systemic alert instead of a wave of individual retries and pages.

const t = $json;
return [{ json: { text: `:fire: *Failure storm detected* -- ${t.distinct_workflow_count} different workflows failed in the last poll window (${t.total_failed} executions total). Suppressing individual auto-retries this cycle to avoid pile-on; likely a shared dependency outage. Investigate before the next cycle retries.` } }];

nodes.name: Classify Failure
nodes.notes: Classification is a best-effort keyword match on the error message/status, not a guaranteed-correct taxonomy -- flagged in the README as the thing to replace with real per-integration error typing in production.

nodes.name: Workflow Still Active?
nodes.notes: Someone may have deliberately deactivated a broken workflow while fixing it -- the monitor shouldn't keep retrying or paging on something a human already took offline on purpose.

parameters.jsCode:
const t = $json;
return [{ json: { execution_id: t.execution_id, workflow_id: t.workflow_id, outcome: 'skipped_inactive_workflow' } }];

nodes.name: Compute Incident Key
nodes.notes: Keyed by workflow + failed node + failure type, not the raw execution id -- every retry creates a brand-new execution id, so tracking retry counts and cooldowns by execution id would reset state on every single attempt.

nodes.name: Get Retry State
nodes.notes: A 404 here is the normal, expected shape for a brand-new incident, not an error -- handled explicitly downstream rather than treated as a failed lookup.

nodes.name: Decide Action
nodes.notes: Permanent and unknown failures never get an automatic retry -- retrying a deterministic bug or an unrecognized failure mode just delays the human who actually needs to look at it, and can mask the real problem.

nodes.name: Update Retry State (Dispatched)
nodes.notes: Exponential backoff (5m / 15m / 45m) plus a little jitter, so a burst of simultaneously-failing executions for the same incident don't all retry in perfect lockstep and hammer the destination again at the same instant.

nodes.name: Within Cooldown?
nodes.notes: 30-minute alert cooldown per incident -- a workflow stuck failing every 5-minute poll cycle gets one page, not six, until it either recovers or the cooldown lapses.

nodes.name: Get Open Incidents
nodes.notes: Recovery is checked every cycle regardless of whether this cycle found any new failures -- a workflow can quietly heal between polls, and closing that loop (not just opening incidents) is the other half of 'self-healing'.

nodes.name: Record Last Checked Timestamp
nodes.notes: Only advances the watermark on a fully-completed cycle -- the degraded path earlier explicitly skips this, so a monitor outage re-checks the same window next time instead of silently skipping it.
